gaps: Zero fish or seafood in the rotation despite a Big Green Egg and cast iron that beg for it.
No East Asian cuisine beyond a single stir-fry noodle dish — no Japanese, no Korean, no Sichuan.
Pork appears once but only in dumplings; it is underdeveloped as a standalone protein.
North African and Moroccan cooking is completely absent.
North Indian cooking is limited to one South Indian kanji; no creamy dal, no paneer dishes.
Weekend project slots are empty — everything skews quick or one-pot with no real technique stretch.
The beef dish (birria) is a long braise; a fast, high-heat beef technique is missing.

ideas.title: Vegan Mapo Tofu
ideas.why: Fills the Sichuan gap and the tofu-protein gap in one wok dish the whole table — including the vegetarian — can eat as written.

ideas.title: Japchae (Sweet Potato Starch Noodles Stir-Fried with Vegetables)
ideas.why: Opens Korean cuisine entirely, adds glass noodles as a new carb format, and works vegetarian by simply omitting meat.

ideas.title: Vegetarian Japanese Curry
ideas.why: Brings Japanese cuisine into the rotation for the first time using a homemade roux — a technique they have never touched — and feeds the vegetarian adult as written.

ideas.title: Dal Makhani
ideas.why: Stretches the Indian repertoire beyond South Indian kanji into slow-cooked North Indian cooking with black lentils and kidney beans — completely vegetarian and Big Green Egg-smokeable.

ideas.title: Moroccan Fish Tagine
ideas.why: Closes two gaps simultaneously — fish as a protein and Moroccan cuisine — using the Dutch oven they already own and a chermoula herb-spice paste that is a completely new technique.

ideas.title: Ultra-Smashed Cheeseburger
ideas.why: Adds a fast, high-heat cast-iron beef technique that is completely different from the long birria braise — maximizing Maillard crust, a skill the household does not yet have in the burger format.
